chapter: Royal Roost, Birdland and Three O'Clock High
title: Miles Davis and the Audubon Ballroom Sundays
summary: Collins brought Miles to play a Sunday and was accused of cheating him; the concerts at the Audubon paid scale and Collins watched the money.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: on the dope, you know. And I got him to play one Sunday. I had to go and get him, take him by my house, have my wife to feed him, had to rent a horn for him, and we played this -- he played this thing this Sunday and he saw all these people here, and I paid him and he said, John, you mother-fucker mother, you trying to cheat me out of my -- you see I drew all these people in here. I said, Miles, all of these people are in here (unintelligible) comp tickets, which they had. I was giving out complimentary tickets to get these people in here. I'd get Bud Powell -- every Sunday we would just have all the, you know just anybody that wasn't working would come up there and work. And we would give them scale, it was always scale, you know.
But if it was anything over -- I don't know, whatever it was they got it. But we weren't charging anything hardly to get in there, you know, just --

The Audubon Ballroom. That was like 168th and Broadway, and we got that -- the guy let us have the hall for little or nothing, because he had the bar, the owner, so he's the only one that made any money. You know, he wouldn't give us part of the bar. But he would give us the door. Well you know, we didn't make anything off the door work because we had to have placards, and I used to work and put

these signs up through Brooklyn and New York. I had bunions and -- but incidentally, half of the time most of the guys would want me to play with them, you know, and they'd want Art to play. Well, Art would go up and play, but I had to watch that money because I knew Art, you know, he was -- I was responsible to the people, you know, to the creditors, I should say. So I'd have to stay there and watch this money, but it would always hit on me to come and play.
